facts.text: The constructor creates the low-level XPS client, calls connect, and keeps the group and stage dictionaries the controller reports
connect opens a TCP connection with TCP_ConnectToServer, logs in, reads the firmware version and calls read_systemini
read_systemini reads the group and stage names from system.ini and then reads each stage's maximum velocity/acceleration and user travel limits from the controller
get_stage_position calls GroupPositionCurrentGet for one element and returns the value
move_stage sends GroupMoveAbsolute, or GroupMoveRelative when relative is true, with the value in a one-element list
get_group_status returns the GroupStatusStringGet text for every group
get_hardware_status returns the PositionerHardwareStatusStringGet text for every stage
get_positioner_errors returns the PositionerErrorStringGet text for every stage, and 'OK' when the text is empty
get_tuning returns a dictionary of the twelve PID and feed-forward parameters of a stage
home_group runs GroupHomeSearch, initializing the group first when its status says it is not initialized
enable_group calls GroupMotionEnable and disable_group calls GroupMotionDisable
abort_group calls GroupMoveAbort for the given group, or for the trajectory group when no group is given
The low-level XPS transport sets a 3600 s socket timeout before each command
The README lists moving stages and groups, homing, setting stage velocity, running trajectories and reading the gathering file among the supported operations

operator_required.name: move_stage
operator_required.reason: no text of the clone states the travel range of a stage: read_systemini reads the user travel limits from the controller configuration at run time (newportxps/newportxps.py:250-253), and a position is in the controller's user units, whose physical meaning (mm or deg) depends on the installed stage. The operator supplies the range of the installed stage in controller user units.
